courses.biggestGap: Cone Canyon and Saltpan Bypass have no chapters — captured at 22%, 50% and 78% of the same lap they are the same picture (same tarmac, same verge, same barrier run, same horizon, same light), so a whole lap of the cup's opener and its longest course passes without the place ever changing, while Switchback Summit does exactly this right (valley floor y=14.5 → mid-mountain traverse with pines and a drop y=68.2 → summit works y=114.2) and proves the roster knows how.
courses.directive: Give Cone Canyon and Saltpan Bypass the three-chapter treatment Switchback Summit already has, and fix the one set piece that tries. Concretely: (1) Saltpan Bypass is 3,952 m of driven line at y=3.1→2.8→2.5 with an unchanging white-flat/black-ribbon/pale-sky frame — the 640 m BYPASS straight is ~12 s of holding accelerate with nothing to look at. Cut it into named chapters the way ring.ts already lets you: run the CAUSEWAY section up onto a raised deck with the pan visibly below both sides, put the CONTRAFLOW through a walled works cutting that encloses the road, and leave the PAN section open — three different spaces, each recognisable from a single frame. Cone Canyon likewise: T2 DIGGERS ELBOW at width 19 should be a cutting between rock walls, not the same open verge as PIT STRAIGHT. (2) The brine patches on Saltpan render as two flat translucent quads floating above the road: their ruled edges cross the tarmac at an angle unrelated to the road, overhang the yellow edge line onto the verge, and show road speckle through them with no waterline, foam, depth or spray (see /tmp/rc2/saltpan-bypass/racing.png and overhead.png). Clamp every 'brine' patch's latFrom/latTo inside ±1.0 so a sheet cannot spill off the road, and file a change against track/road.ts for the sheet's lift and its edge treatment — a puddle needs a darker rim and a specular, not a coloured pane hovering over the crown. (3) Not yours but blocking: a grey drum-on-a-disc prop hovers unsupported in the sky beside the mesas in every Cone Canyon frame I captured (three of three) and reads as a flying saucer, and a light mast lies flat on the ground beside an upright one on the quarry (/tmp/rc2/jackhammer-quarry/far.png) — raise both with world/landprops.ts and world/place.ts. (4) The field loses real time stuck on your surfaces: on Saltpan, racers spend 55.4 s under 12 m/s per 130 s of racing and one reversed 104 m over 8 s in sand at (706, 232); on the quarry, T3 THE CRUSHER and the 10 m-radius section drop the AI to 3.1 and 5.2 m/s. Pull the sand bands back off the racing line or widen the run-off so a mistake costs a second, not a lap.
evidence: Drove all four courses through window.__GAME and reconstructed the real driven line (0.1 s samples, 2 laps each). Plotted silhouettes: dogleg / comb / wedge / hourglass — genuinely un-confusable, so round 1's 'four drawings of the same object' finding is fixed. Measured per lap: cone-canyon 2,561 m, R<40m 67 m, longest straight 327 m, elevation 28 m, aspect 2.37; jackhammer-quarry 2,534 m, R<40m 328 m, straight 205 m, elevation 42.8 m; saltpan-bypass 3,952 m, straight 708 m, elevation 13.8 m; switchback-summit 2,773 m, straight 221 m, elevation 116.2 m.

Captured the same chase view at 22%, 50% and 78% of one lap on each course (/tmp/journey). Cone Canyon: y=12.8 / 13.0 / 2.1 — three near-identical frames, same orange verge, same red-and-white striped fence, same tan cone hills, same sky; with the minimap covered you cannot say which third of the lap you are on. Saltpan Bypass: y=3.1 / 2.8 / 2.5 — same white salt, same black ribbon with a yellow line, same single distant butte, three times. Jackhammer Quarry: y=-16.3 / -41.2 / -13.2 — frame 2 shows a highwall, frames 1 and 3 are the same open bench. Switchback Summit: y=14.5 / 68.2 / 114.2 — valley floor, then a traverse with pines and a guard rail over a drop, then the summit works. Only one of four courses has chapters.

/tmp/rc2/saltpan-bypass/racing.png and overhead.png: THE FLOOD draws as two overlapping flat translucent quads (teal and lavender) sitting visibly above the tarmac at different heights. Their edges are ruled straight lines that cut across the lane at an angle unrelated to the road and continue past the yellow edge line onto the salt verge. Road speckle is visible through them. No waterline, no foam, no depth gradient, no spray, no wake. From directly overhead the near sheet terminates in a hard straight line mid-lane. This is the roster's only mechanic that changes how the road behaves and it is the worst-looking thing in the cup.

perf.biggestGap: On a failing machine the emergency `collapseSeam()` path installs the seam-held content levers with no moment gate, so the start-line grandstands empty from packed to bare grey terracing under the "3" of the countdown — the exact regression the file's own seam rule was written to fix, on the one camera-locked frame in the game with nothing to hide it behind, and the repo's own `tools/perfgate.mjs` prints `FAIL: 2 change(s) inside a sealed phase: countdown,countdown` and photographs it.
perf.directive: Put `collapseSeam()` behind the same moment gate as the ordinary path: on a rung collapse, install the frame-half immediately (that is what rescues the frame and my mid() walk proves it is invisible — the stand is still packed at mid(6)) but keep `crowd`, `aa` and `drawDistance` deferred through `countdown`/`finished`/`results` and let them land on the next real seam. It costs the failing machine nothing measurable: I isolated the whole seam-held half at 718ms -> 715.3ms at the floor (0.4%) and 1798.5ms -> 1729.4ms at the top (3.8%), against 60.1% for the resolution lever it travels with — so holding it for a three-second countdown buys back the game's most-watched frame for under half a percent. Verify by re-running `node tools/perfgate.mjs` unmodified until it prints `PASS: no change landed in countdown/finished/results/loading` and the ceremony verdict reads a single rung value. Two secondary items while you are in there: (1) `src/core/quality.ts` states at its `quality:changed` emit that "`ui/menus/stage.ts` sizes its own set off this event" — stage.ts contains no `bus.on` of any kind and reads `ctx.quality.shadows` once as a build-time const, so that justification is false and contradicts the file's own §7 note; fix the comment and raise the one-line `Math.min(1, 1200 / w) * scale` request against `src/ui/menus/stage.ts` as a blocking cross-module ask, because the title screen is still the most expensive surface in the product and the ladder is architecturally barred from it. (2) Nothing in `src/ui/**` exposes a graphics/quality/resolution control — the only door is `globalThis.__QUALITY` — so a player whose picture has been permanently halved (rung 6 written to localStorage under a hardware key) cannot see it, refuse it, or clear it; publish the standing rung as a settable preference on ctx and file the settings-screen request against `src/ui/menus`.
evidence: THE DEFECT, PHOTOGRAPHED: /tmp/perfgate/pressure-countdown-r0-t75.7.png vs pressure-countdown-r6-t83.3.png — identical camera, identical "3" numeral, identical grid. At rung 0 both grandstands are packed five rows deep with hundreds of individually-coloured spectators; at rung 6, 7.6s later with the governor on auto, both are bare grey decking with empty seat rails and the bunting hanging over nobody. Cropped 3x to /tmp/perfgate/stand-r0.png and stand-r6.png. The resolution did NOT change between them (both 1600x900, `sc=1` in the probe) — only the population did.

`node tools/perfgate.mjs`, unmodified, exits with: `--- pressure verdict: rungs seen during ceremony = 0,6 (must be a single value) ---` and `FAIL: 2 change(s) inside a sealed phase: countdown,countdown`. The change log carries `{"from":0,"to":6,"why":"collapsed (64x budget) x6","phase":"countdown","deferred":"scale,crowd,aa,drawDistance"}` — the governor's own automatic six-rung collapse landing inside the ceremony. (The tool prints FAIL but still exits 0, so nothing is actually gated on it.)

The mid-race path is CLEAN and deserves credit: my own grandstand walk (/tmp/crowd/stand-mid6.png vs stand-set6.png) on the frozen countdown frame shows `mid(6)` — the whole frame-half at scale 0.5 — leaves the stand fully packed, `crowdLive` staying at 1 across mid(0..6) while `crowd` falls 1 -> 0.16. Everything the governor may spend while the player is watching is genuinely invisible. Only the seam install empties it.
